[strike] 相当重复且无聊 [/strike] 开发者回我了所以我又尝试了一下，和我的评论一致的是武器确实很好玩，一口气通关了。risky分支的每次打开游戏都可以改难度的设定很有帮助，别的细节上的差异感觉是有但是又不敢确定。第一次玩的时候可能是不小心，选的难度比较高，玩着玩着甚至忘了还有难度设定这一回事，但是说实话这个跟hurt me plenty在同一位置的那个难度确实还是比普通难度高很多。打完一整局之后再调整build的感觉比在局中死掉回来改装备更有爽感一点，这也是我为什么推荐在较低难度游玩。其实有不少很能给人留下深刻印象的情景，但是需要通关五次还是让这些体验有点过于分散，感觉三次比较合适（？）也不会太少导致没有改build的空间。所以其实是值得一玩的。

虽然我还没打完，但是我觉得也差不多可以给个大致的评价了: [h2] 相当重复，所以无聊 [/h2] 因为你主线是需要重复通关，但是你这个关卡长度太长了，且有几张地图还是固定的，玩到后面就是直接跑到固定隐藏点拿钱，然后速跑到关卡末尾，一顿突突给boss秒了就到下一关了，实在是无聊 且角色rouge元素太少了，build有点太平淡了，也就前期需要稍微考量一下，但是只要你捡到轮椅了，那你只需要花钱解锁了之后，就能直接开局获得了，那我觉得别的枪存在感好像也没那么强了 然后高难度的话玩起来就太恶心了，因为是rouge，敌人是随机的，敌人数量也是随机的，roll到几个司马怪就没法跑了，你一跑就被群殴，只能嗯打，并且也因为是高难度，打完之后也没什么收益，所以后面我都是开低难度耍的，不然有点纯粹找罪受了 关卡设计的话，还是有点意思的，跑起来也有点意思，前提是你不需要以通关游戏为目的重复好几遍去游玩，但是现实如此，实在是太冗长了；然后有隐藏点，但是这游戏后面探索隐藏地点有点太正常化了，因为你不找的话，打怪获取的金钱量是完全不够你在局内局外瞎b花的，找了的话就有点开无敌模式了，感觉还是需要平衡一下 最后是美术，虽然我很喜欢这种80-90年代的封面欺诈+90-00年代那种亚文化风格，但是游戏内不统一+过于粗糙的美术我是不太能接受的，整的有点太粗糙了，一块一块的 等晚点打完再重新看看吧，我现在是啃不下去了
食之无味弃之可惜，音乐和艺术风格有趣但是游戏玩法实在是无聊

I feel kinda mixed about this game. In one hand, the weapons feel punchy, the action is satisfying and the gunplay is good. But on the other hand, its not a regular shooter, its a time attack roguelite that manages to be extremely repetitive. I played several runs and at first I had some fun. It wasn't doing anything new, but everything felt good enough. The weapons feel great, they sound good, they have a nice kick and most feel effective. With some rare ones (mainly melee and the flamethrower), I liked using most weapons. Visually, the game looks ok. Regular low poly models with low resolution textures akin to a PS1/N64 game. But I think the game plays too safe. It has a bunch of innuendos and adult adjacent imagery, but its all barely above a teen rating. Even the violence is pretty light with no gore, nothing aside some blood particles. There is a lot of underwear and covered breasts. That all the "adult themes" you get. There is a nice variation of enemies, but they all seem to play the same. Some beeline to you and melee, some stay away and shoot one specific gun. The AI is very stupid and more often than not I found it stuck on a corner besides a door without knowing what to do. Now the main problem I have with this game: its not a linear, mission/level based shooter, but a time attack roguelite. You start the run with a weapon you purchased, then run through 5 maps and fight a boss. The first issue was that these maps keep repeating. Out of these 5 maps, 3 were the EXACT same city block, down to the same enemies and item placement. When after I defeated the first boss and went to level 2, the same maps showed up again. There are some different maps now and then, but every run seemed to go the exact same way. You can enable checkpoints by storing your money on machines at the start of every map, but this is only good once. If you die and use the checkpoint, you need to store money in a different one, or you will have to restart the run. Which is how I found out after starting from a checkpoint that put me in the middle of 8 enemies with only the starting pistol and I got immediately juiced like an overripe orange. The "time attack" part comes from an advancing wall, not unlike one from a battle royale game. If it overtakes you, you lose health until you move away or die. This means you have a time limit to finish the levels, you can't explore, you can't backtrack and you can trap yourself on some rooms without secondary routes. The upgrades feel a little limited and unlocking new weapons doesn't helps much if you start with so little ammo. And the character is a bit annoying. She has no personality other than swearing, complaining and going "woah awesome!" at random stuff, her voice doesn't sounds tough, sounds like a teenager posing as a tough guy on the internet. Like a certain fictional character once said: "Swearing doesn't makes you cool." If this was a regular shooter with properly designed and structured levels, I think I have enjoyed it more. But as it is, it feels like a missed opportunity. Also, no one but brazilian people will get the joke in the title. Basically, it would be something like "Sona Bith Samurai"

I was really on the fence about wether this was going to be a positive or negative review because theres a lot to like about the game but ultimately it's just not very fun. Having a handful of maps that you have to go through potentially 20-50+ times per map it gets stale after like the 2-3rd run through the same map with the same enemies.... It also has this whole adult aesthetics but goes to deep into it to not cater to people who doesnt like adult stuff in their games and doesnt go deep enough into it to cater to who the devs should have catered to. It essentially end up catering to no one attempting to cater to everyone.... Overall the game really just feels like an EXTREMELY waterede down version of Nightmare reaper and is ultimately worse in every way.

I really wish I could recommend this game, for the pixel art and general presentation of it are really well done. However, the level design is very lazily made and it pretty much requires you to repeat the same 4-5 stages over and over again, making the game feel rather tedious after 1-2 hours of play.

Some fun elements but a significant lack of movement options dampens the gameplay experience a bit, and the way your guns are inventoried is a bit weird. I think some people could really get into this, the shooting is simple and snappy and feels decent, but it's a bit lacking for me. What really kills the game though is it doesn't lean into the perverted elements enough and isn't violent enough - which normally I don't care about in a game one way or another, but when it's.....this.....and you play it and it's PG-13 at best it's a bit of a let down. The whole aesthetic wrapper here is a pissed off girlfriend tearing through hordes of digital cat girls and succubi, but it really doesn't actually deliver on that like at all and is suuuuper tame. So now it's just lost in a sea of mediocre rogue like FPS games because it didn't even leverage the one thing that made it stand out.

This game is fun but it has some issues, I'll list them in order of severity and suggest some fixes, I'm fine with doing some work on my end if you're willing to compensate me for it, namely in audio balance. 1. Audio Balance is terrible, like bad-terrible instead of powerful-terrible. First off, any sound that has a proximity effect that is localized on the player should not have that and should just be reduced by 50%. Liza's Voice is fine, might need a 10-20% reduction but overall it's fine. Music needs to be reduced by around 70% just because it's too loud, same goes for the Sound effects slider, but... Weapon switch and firing sounds are especially problematic. Merchant Voice Lines are too loud, I have to put the Voice Volume Slider to 20% of normal for it to be good, but then I can't hear enemies unless they're close enough to spoon me into oblivion. Ambient Sounds also need to be reduced to 50%. I ultimately want enemy voice sounds to remain just where they are or close to it, but everything else to be put down a good 5+ db if not 15 (or so it feels like). Any attempt to properly balance via sliders just makes the game feel muffled at times and I don't like having to do that as a new player. 2. Enemy Visibility is very low in dark areas which feel like they shouldn't be as dark as they are, as a result it's rather easy to just not see some enemies and take free hits. I'd just like all enemies to simply have a subtle glow around them, like a less-intense version of the way humans and predators appear to alien players without their special monochromatic-fullbright vision mode in AVP 1. Even with a very thin bright outline around enemies would be perfect. Or maybe environments could just not be so damn dark half of the time. 3. I don't know if it's placebo, but the camera feels a bit odd, even with it on 90 FOV, it feels like I'm still more zoomed-in than I should be but it might just be me not having played an FPS in a while and this isn't really an issue that's too bad. That's about it, I like the game and how s*xually-frustrated some parts of it feel, it's great and honestly makes me want to make something like it and I really really like the roguelike elements and unlockables of it too. I know I'll love this game, just... please for the love of god balance the audio at the very least.

This is a decent game that plays well, but you should go play Nightmare Reaper instead, it does everything this game does but better. The rest of this is just a stream of consciousness review: It is fun for the first few hours, but quickly becomes very repetitive. This game is structured like a rouguelite with meta progression and changing runs. The meta progression is okay, but the randomization of the world is really poor. The world is split into areas and connectors, with the connectors being a bunch of randomized buildings slapped together in pretty boring configurations. The areas are pretty neat, but they are the exact same every time with only the enemies changing. Having to run through the same areas a minimum of 5 times to beat the game is not really fun. The only thing that really changes on the different runs is the ending, and if you die in the ending you have to restart at the last checkpoint. Which may screw you over if you don't have enough stuff unlocked cause you will start with only your basic weapons.

Look, it might be a borderline gooner game, and it might have several notable flaws (pretty janky, limited upgrades, very repetitive structure) but I had a lot of fun! The core gameply felt very satisfying to me. I've played hundreds of games but this might be the first FPS, and I'm sure it wasn't a perfect representation of the genre but I thought the levels were really well-designed, there were plenty of varied weapons to play with, and I liked finding the secret areas building my collections enough to 100% the whole game. There's also a very detailed world outside the main gameplay loop: I especially loved the cozy house that got bigger every couple acts, and there's quite a few minigames too, all of which are cute but there's definitely a couple duds amongst them. I also thought the fact that enemies in different factions fight each other was a great touch, I love seeing things like that considered in games. I didn't pay much attention to the story as it was happening, but I liked where it wound up. I'd also like to shout out the Steam Deck yet again: this is the first game I've tried out gyro controls with and they work amazing, I don't think they're even designed to be in this game but combined with the back buttons I had a pretty incredible flow of play for a controller.

Very nice. This game is a tastefully risque (but no longer NSFW) boomer shooter that has a lot of roguelite elements. You have the option to enable random levels when exiting the hub/beginning the game, but the traditional gameplay loop revolves around navigating the same set of levels repeatedly, with each one being subtly rearranged (Items, enemies, etc.) - When you get to the end of the levels, you fight a boss or encounter an event that THEN adds an additional map to the end of the levels. So, the general progression will be: Enter level for the first time, kill a bunch of enemies followed by the boss, and get spat back to the Hub knowing that there's more at the end of that journey. While this is all occuring, you earn money that can be spent on starting weapons, cosmetics and even anime figurines to display in the hub that provide benefits. Simple format that is admittedly repetitive, but the low price, satisfying weapons, and presentation of the game keeps me entertained. While Strafe is hated for its randomized levels; this one is unapologetically hated for its handcrafted levels, but to me it feels like they pretty much made a better version of that game. It's surprisingly fun shooting cartoonishly lewd anime girls, I must say.

Fida Puti Samurai is a rougelike Doom clone, I mean, Boomer Shooter. You're playing a VR game fighting hoards of ladies. This is a fun game... for the first few hours. It really suffers due to being a rouge-like. There are 3 levels and each level containing 1 of 13 maps, the order of which gets shuffled each run. The layouts of these maps are not randomized, but what is randomized is the alleyways that connect the maps. Because this is a rouge-like you will likely die a lot, and when you do you will need to go through the same levels over and over again. It reminds me of a similar boomer shooter I played called STRAFE! Similarly it was a rouge-like where you would repeat the same levels over and over. The benefit FPS... I just realized it's name can be shorted to sound like the term FPS, clever. FPS avoids this issue by being snapier and having a more weapon variety than STRAFE. Each enemy you kill will drop a weapon. The starting weapons are pretty bad but as you progress the enemies will drop better weapons. The gameplay loop on its own isn't bad. The shooting is a lot of fun and you get some fun weapons to play around with! Multiple weapons have alt fires such as explosive rounds on the single barrel shotgun. A pitch fork that shoots a fire ball that does DoT. Your submachine guns are bullet guzzlers but wow do they sure can tear up enemies, as well as my speakers. I could go on about the myriad of weapons but you get my point. The gameplay is a blast, and the synthwave soundtrack does a great job at putting you in the zone. While I do find the game to be really fun, it can also be rather dull. You're fighting the same enemies, exactly where you expect them to be every time. And combat while fun doesnt evolve much. You can only upgrade weapons during a run but not always as you don't always have access to a shop. But once you do, you're met with a choice. Do I, purchase an upgrade or store my money at a checkpoint which allows me to purchase items at the shop easing future runs and marking a checkpoint allowing me to continue from this spot in the next run. Naturally I tend to choose the later, the former only being worthwhile if you can take the risk. I just dont find the upgrades to be all that worth while usually. They dont change your movement options other than the double jump. The weapons upgrades are for small gains like increasing accuracy or armor piercing. Oh, and these upgrades are attached to your one weapon, so dont lose it. Strangely this game allows you to pick up everything. You can carry the same weapon 20 over if you want it's strange why dont restrict you to one of a kind because you can be trying to pick up one weapon and grab another by mistake just because they're right beside each other. Another frustrating mechanic is the green wall of doom. It's a wall that presses in closer to you to incentivize you to play the level faster. Which I dont like! It's such an arbitrary reason to stop you from fully exploring each level because they want you to replay these levels and uncover a secret area on the next run since you'll be more inclined to want to try something different the next time. I do enjoy the game but it can get really exhausting, very quickly. Truth be told, I couldn’t complete a run. I would get to the final level and die on some ridiculously powerful group of enemies. When I would restart from my checkpoint, I lacked the resources needed to fight back and would quickly fail. And when you die, you go back to the first level all over again. This is why I got so bored so quickly! The loop of overcoming the level, getting to where I was, getting overwhelmed by the enemies and restarting back to square one drove me up a wall. I do enjoy this game, and do recommend it but I’d recommend it in short bursts or 3 run sessions as to avoid burning out.

Fida Puti isn’t a bad game but it sure isn’t a good one either. There is fun to be had here but going into it know that: 1) it’s the most padded out game I’ve ever played essentially requiring you to play the same content 4+ times with little variation 2) it’s not a roguelike, it just puts rooms in different orders. Whee 3) it’s UGLY. I don’t know what’s going on with the lightning in this game but enemies are almost always darker than the environments making it real hard to see them 4) something it up with sound mixing where you can only hear things REALLY close to you. So yeah it has massive problems but overall I still had fun with it even if the message at the end was hamfisted and dumb as hell. Lots of cheesecake tho.

Wall closing in on you creates a sense of urgency and the deposit system required to save the money you collect in order to grab upgrades certainly adds to that "one more run" kind of deal. Shared it with some friends and they called it "SUS". I'm out of touch with modern day verbiage and vernacular, but even I can deduce that it is a young person acronym for Some Underrated Stuff. If you like SUS games, fun shooters, or quick loops to run before bed, check it out.

To be clear, players will generally not have reason to reach over 200 hours playing this game. As to why it's that high, we'll get to that point at the bottom A lot of people that play this game are coming from Civvie's short early access review of the game during the 2021 Realms Deep Roundup, and while the game has gone through massive updates since that video, the core gameplay remains the same. This is a boomer shooter that focuses on goods guns and no-frills running to stay alive. The game is decidedly simplistic with its controls, so there's no dashing, no grappling hook, almost no gun has a scope, and your shotgun doesn't reload faster from swapping to another weapon. There are means for getting faster movement speed and even double jump, but that's it. If the movement feels sluggish, try maxing out FOV to 120 in the options menu. Max FOV really just feels like zooming out as there doesn't seem to be much of any perspective warping, and you will feel a lot faster. Also, if you're having trouble seeing if you hit the enemy, just turn on 'view damage numbers,' its consistent with the 'playing in someone's vr' setting of the game, anyway. For enemies, if its a humanoid enemy, its carrying a weapon, and if its carrying a weapon, it can be generally be picked up. Aside from very specific edge cases, whatever the enemies use against the player will make up the majority of the player's inventory. Enemy variety is separated by factions, such as punks, zombies, aliens, and so on. Each faction only uses certain guns, so after a while you'll know what kind of firepower is going to be dropped based on the first enemy you see in an area. While enemy factions have their preferred guns, all the expected types of guns from any fps are in the game, from various pistols to shotguns to rifles and rocket launchers. Practically every weapon feels nice for one fact: every weapon does good damage. While Large enemies and bosses exist that will take a good number of rounds to drop, most of the mobs go down in 2 to 4 shots depending on the difficulty level. A note on the five difficulty options, the first two are easy to mess around in and the player can eat a bunch of bullets to the face, and medium difficulty is just that. The 2nd highest difficulty, Mwrrrgh or however it's spelled, is balanced differently than the rest – everything hits harder, including the player, so if damage is still feeling too spongey, this is the way to go. The highest difficulty was tuned for veterans of the genre that don't want to cakewalk the game. Helping the player not get hurt is that there are no hitscan weapons. Different guns have different bullet speeds and you'll often see bullets coming at you midflight. The closest gun to feel like (and might actually be) a hitscan gun is the rail gun, and that's for obvious reasons. Helping give the player an edge over enemies are alt fire methods and the ability to dual wield. Every handgun has an 'akimbo mode': while holding any handgun, from pistols to revolvers, just pick up a copy of the same gun from the floor. You can't mix and match, like have a submachine gun in one hand and revolver in the other, but you can hold two revolver in each hand or two submachine guns. Most of the weapons also has some form of alt fire, from the auto shotguns performing a three-shot burst to the rocket launcher arming a nuke. Whenever you pick up a new weapon, try holding down left click or right click as most weapons have another use to them. Level design can be a love-it-or-hate-it affair because of the game's death wall gimmick. Every stage has the player being chased by a giant green scanwall that insta-kills anything it touches. The wall itself isn't very fast, its really there to prevent the player from backtracking or getting lost, and that second point is important. The levels are designed so the player never gets trapped or lost, so there's never a lagging point during the game – there can be maze-like sections, but if you see the green glowing death wall in front of you, turn around. The game is tagged as a roguelite with random level generation, and that's mostly true. Every stage is broken up between 2 things: street sections, and pre-designed set locations. The street sections may have random shops and the occasional faction fight, but its always wide, linear, and populated by rats and undead. This can sound boring on paper but in practice its pretty fun simply because of how destructible everything is. Cars are parked everywhere ready to blow up and usually have trunk you can kick open to find gas canisters that can be picked up as free bombs, and any green truck with a radioactive sign can be blown up to make gigantic explosions that will vacuum things up nearby before going boom. Enemy factions also hate each other, so occasionally you'll find faction fighting while going through the level. The pre-made locations range from parks to theaters, with their floorplan always being the same. Every location will be encountered in one run, but the order in which you encounter each location is random, along with what enemy faction is currently occupying the area. Keeping locations from feeling redundant are secrets - every location has at least 4 secret areas that have bonuses from having late game guns to having glowing toys that, when shot, let the player buy permanent stat buffs back home. Because the green death wall is always moving forward, its not expected for the player to find every secret in one run, let alone figure out an efficient path to hit every secret whenever they end up in that location again. Character progression in the game comes from going home to buy stuff with the money gained from killing enemies, breaking bags, and opening boxes and lockers during a run. Dying with money on you during a run lets you keep some of the earned cash, so the only secure methods of bringing money home is to stuff them in mailboxes that are randomly placed on the streets, or successfully finishing a run. Money can also be used to buy buffs during a run from smoking vending machines, so there's a number of money sinks if you're swimming in cash. Players can only buy stuff at home that's unlocked during a run, and different conditions gives access to new things. As said earlier, shooting hidden glowing toys gives access to buying permanent stat boosts like more health or more ammo on pickup. If you bought a weapon rack, picking up a new weapon during a run makes it purchasable back home, letting the player bring whatever gun they've found before as the starting weapon for the next run. Buying a closet lets you buy outfits and different armor that are all found randomly in bags marked 'stuff,' and these change max armor health, changing ammo capacity, as well as changing player appearance. Just to keep expectations set, this is not a porn game. Sure, its lewd and filled with kink, innuendo, and cheesecake, but don't expect to find anything here to play the game one-handed for. The developer was greatly influenced by classic 3D Realms games, so aside from a few looping animations playing on in-game tvs, don't expect anything much more sexually intense than what's found in classic Shadow Warrior or Duke Nukem 3D. What you see in the trailer is as deep as it gets. If you read this far or just skipped to the bottom, players will finish this game in about 10 hours or less depending on difficulty level. On a dollar-per-game time basis, 12 bucks isn't a bad price point. If you feel weak or stuck, mess around with the options and interact with things by kicking them. That all said, why is my playtime over 200 hours? Because the developer listens to feedback and keeps updating the game. Throughout the entire early access process and ever since Civvie's mini review, the developer had been releasing an update patch on an almost weekly basis. If you can get it dirt cheap and don't mind a little hentai mixed into your FPS, it's okay for a little while. It's set up a bit like a roguelike, though only in that you try to proceed through a few main areas, each with a series of themed stages and split up by power-up substages. You fight the same few enemies types over and over, and the layouts of each stage is the same, though you can randomize the order. You earn money you can use to buy single-run powerups at very specific locations, buy checkpoints, or to bank for picking up items in the "real world", such as starting with the pump action shotgun or light machine gun. Probably the most novel thing here is the wall of death that follows you through a level. It's a weirdly awesome way to tell you you're heading in the wrong direction and keep you on pace. But every boss is killed in two to four explosive ammo hits (single shot shotgun alt fire grenade is crazy damaging, rocket launcher is faster but less damaging), and just headshotting everything with a shotgun is a viable play method. Pick up a sniper type weapon such as the railgun or pipe rifle and kill everything in the city sub-levels from max draw distance. Nothing else to it. Beat the game once and you restart with a new Magical Girl thing going on. I haven't explored this part at all yet, because it just makes me have to fight all the same boring stuff again. I don't care anymore. Competent enough in feel, but needs more going on. Copy pasted rooms and assets suck.

[h1] Fida Puti Samurai: перспективный, но сырой проект [/h1] Fida Puti Samurai ощущается как альфа-версия чего-то действительно интересного. Кор-геймплей затягивает, но всё время не покидает ощущение, что игре чего-то не хватает. И не хватает в первую очередь контента: разнообразных видов одежды, уникального оружия, интерактивных объектов на аренах. Формально они есть, но их настолько мало, что они просто не запоминаются. Баланс в игре в целом интересный, но у боссов он попросту сломан: их можно уничтожить меньше чем за минуту. Карт тоже очень мало — когда в третий раз проходишь одну и ту же городскую локацию, это начинает утомлять. Кроме того, не раскрыт потенциал механик, связанных с домом, комнатами, видеоиграми и контентом на CD-дисках. Пока это лишь недоработанные элементы, которые могли бы сделать игру гораздо глубже. Система оружия кажется скучной. У игрока может быть пулемёт и винтовка, но различие между ними сводится лишь к цифрам урона. То же самое можно сказать и про большую часть арсенала. Темп игры тоже вызывает вопросы: если в Echo Point Nova ты можешь подстроить его под себя, а в Selaco он ощущается чётко, то в Fida Puti Samurai он какой-то невнятный — медленный, но при этом пытается выдавить из себя чё то динамичное. Отдельная проблема — баги. Вот примеры как небольших, так и критических ошибок: [list] [*]Если зайти в игру и во время заставки нажать F1, вместо самой игры появится рабочий стол ПК персонажа без скайбокса и без возможности управления. [*]В какой-то момент игра начинает сильно лагать, как будто теряются кадры. Эта проблема наблюдается не только у меня и остаётся нерешённой уже больше [b]4 месяцев [/b]. Единственное временное решение — ограничение в 60 FPS, но примерно через час игры потери кадров всё равно начинают появляться, хоть и в меньшей степени. [/list] На данный момент Fida Puti Samurai не стоит своих денег, но при этом мне даже немного стыдно её возвращать. В проекте есть масса интересных идей и задумок, но он пока ощущается недоделанным. Тем не менее, я с нетерпением жду обновлений и фиксов — за такими проектами всё равно интересно следить. [hr][/hr] [h1] Fida Puti Samurai: A Promising but Unfinished Project [/h1] Fida Puti Samurai feels like an alpha version of something genuinely interesting. The core gameplay is engaging, but there's always a lingering sense that something is missing. And what's missing is content: more clothing options, unique weapons, and interactive objects during fights. Technically, some of these things exist, but they are so scarce that you barely notice them. The game’s balance is intriguing, but the bosses are completely broken—you can defeat them in less than a minute. The number of maps is also disappointingly low. By the third time you play through the same city level, it starts feeling repetitive and exhausting. Additionally, there’s untapped potential in the mechanics related to the house, rooms, video games, and CD-based content. Right now, these elements feel underdeveloped, but they could add significant depth to the game. The weapon system is another weak spot. You might have an SMG and a rifle, but in reality, they only differ in raw damage numbers. This issue applies to most of the player’s arsenal. The game's pacing is also a bit off—unlike Echo Point Nova, where you can adjust it to your liking, or Selaco, where the flow is well-defined, Fida Puti Samurai feels sluggish yet oddly tries to force a sense of dynamism. There are also plenty of minor and critical bugs, such as: [list] [*]If you start the game and press F1 during the intro, instead of loading into the game, you’ll see the player's in-game desktop with no skybox and no ability to control anything. [*]At some point, the game starts experiencing severe frame drops, making it feel laggy. This issue has persisted for over [b] 4 months [/b] and affects multiple players. The only temporary fix is limiting the game to 60 FPS, but even then, frame drops return after about an hour of gameplay, albeit less frequently. [/list] Right now, Fida Puti Samurai isn't worth its current price, but I still feel guilty about refunding it. There are plenty of fascinating ideas and concepts, but in its current state, the game feels incomplete. That said, I’ll be keeping an eye on updates and fixes—projects like this are always interesting to follow.

I like this game. Note that I would count my full playtime lower the the stated 20 hours since I have had this game for a while and reset it now and then after some updates to start from the beginning. My current safe I would more estimate around 5 to 7 hours in. I bought all currently available alternative starting weapons, and have roughly 3 complete armor sets. There seems to be more hidden in that regard as well as a load of mini figures that supposedly can be found during runs, of which I have found three At the core the game works as follows: You enter the level and fight forward trough it while being pursued by a digital green wall. The wall was never too much of an issue for me. For every kill you get money. You can find money in a few secret but easily findable hideouts. If you have a minimum of 500 Bucks you can activate checkpoints and deposit all your current money. If you die (or make it "trough" but I'll get to that) you can invest money in between your attempts in armor or alternative starting weapons. Even on the lower difficulties you will be quickly toast if you just run forward mindlessly. The exploration is minimal and after you figure out how to find them they become a routine way to stock up on ammo, health, armor and money. The wall was never a problem in this regard, The game has a peculiar atmosphere and story going, It has a bit off a feeling of Homestuck, an early Internet-alternative-storytelling-phenomena. Its purposely garish and oversexualised in that 80s Anime way and the home hub feels quite eerie. I am not sure if I like the protagonist girl. She seems to be quite unnecessarily irate and aggressive towards someone that seems to care about and support her. But maybe the story will redeem her in some way. Its interesting at least and as another character said: "Lets see how deep this hole goes." The soundmix is all over the place just as other reviews have stated. It is just a bit messy and even when messing with the sound sliders it never feels quite right. Guns however sound appropriately, satisfying and depending on what you use. The controls also feels quite raw. As in; there are not flourishes to the controls and the overall physics, your own as well as those of the enemies. However that comes out to a game that precisely takes your inputs as you give it. Aiming is up to you and your knowledge as to how the different weapons work and how their projectiles fly. Now why the thumbs down? The core concept at the start is you fight, you win, you advance. In my last run I was finally good enough to get trough to one of the latest stages to trigger a storybeat, After said story beat is a fight that I was clearly winning... just for the game to kick me out of it unceremoniously. What really upset me then when within the story beat I was told, "hey lets get back to that stage that we just got kicked out from". I assumed that I would get the option to the start at said stage just to find out that I would have to play the run all over again. So you are telling me I am getting kicked out of my run, due to no fault of my own, just to be told to get there again? That is extremely forced and unnecessary padding and that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. This game doesn't need padding. It doesn't need to crack a certain minimum playtime if it is well done. Strafe (Gold Edition) as well as Mullett Mad Jack, both available here on Steam, show how this concept, including a time limit that chases the player, can be done properly and without that. The issue here is that the game, despite its qualities, is rather short on unique elements and that, as I mentioned before, it lacks any additional unique flourishes when it comes to the actual gameplay. I just have no interest to drudge trough a whole run just to, maybe some a smidge of new additional story. Hence it ultimately gets a thumbs down from me.

[quote]Just saying, but I do have a curator page. If you like my remarks about games, you can find more of them here: https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44130985-TDP%27s-Gaming-Escapades [/quote] I have started to have a more positive opinion of games with adult content in them. In most of these games, the gameplay is either non-existent or is extremely basic on purpose to direct the player towards the adult content as fast as possible, if not immediately. But as of late, I have noticed more and more adult games that have actual effort put into them, making them something I can see myself enjoying. One of those games is Fida Puti Samurai. The game is full of adult waifu imagery and themes, but has forged its gameplay in a way that even after enabling the option to apply censorship, it still feels fun to play. Although only for a limited period of time, as the experience will go downhill the more you play it. [h2]The curse of the homework folder[/h2] Fida Puti Samurai is a game that is clearly inspired by Duke Nukem 3D, and you can see and feel those inspirations as you play through it. To name a few, the main menu of the game replicates the way DN3D's menu looked like (the originals, not greaselord's version), some of the levels directly reference the ones in DN3D as they are very similar in terms of their layouts, and the way the game handles the display of adult imagery also feels similar. Although this time, the latter's inclusion has a reason... a reason which many of us can understand. The game's events start when a programmer develops a virtual app for his girlfriend to get away from real life's hardships. This program transports her to a virtualized isolated cabin in the woods with a snowy setting and chill music playing in the background. Everything is fine, until she finds a bug that allows her to enter a world made from the dude's homework folder contents in the form of a first person shooter and mow down all of his waifus. I'm going to be honest here: This is a creative way to have a reason for the inclusion of adult content, and I like how it intertwines them with the gameplay. Nearly all of the enemies, both human and furry, are dressed in revealing suits. The walls are plastered with questionable posters and graffitis. Some of the ally robots are activated by inserting adult CDs in them. There's even a couple references to a certain treasure-hunting bat, for those whom Sonic Adventure 2 was the start of their sexual awakening. And if you feel uncomfortable or don't want to have all the images around for any reason, you can activate the Neko Plus mode while loading a save file to censor every explicit image with cat pictures. [h2]Feels fun, but...[/h2] I have to say, I did not expect the gameplay to actually be fun. The controls are smooth, the gunplay is enjoyable, the shooting sounds are punchy and there is a variety of weapons available in the game. I also really liked the addition of "Scan Wall" that chases the player and quickly kills them if it catches up, as it increases the speed of gameplay and puts more urgency to decide what to do next and how. However, I do have some big issues with the gameplay. First, the boss fights are pretty easy. You just need a gun with rapid fire capabilities (N19, light machine gun, minigun) or explosive ammo (rocket launcher), and all of them go down quickly. Second, unfortunately the gameplay loses all momentum and becomes monotonous and repetitive after a short while, largely based on the fact that the game tries to be a roguelite, yet does not have the necessities to be one. [h2]I don't think this shoud've been a roguelite...[/h2] Roguelite games heavily rely on replayability. They require you to go through them numerous times, which will take you hours, in order to beat them or reach the desired conclusion. Because of this, there should be enough unique or randomizable content in the game or it will cause fatigue pretty fast, making the players bored and unwilling to continue as despite all advancements, everything would still look the same to them. Sadly, this game is not satisfactory in this regard. The game gets repetitive in about 1-2 hours due to its level structure. Basically, each level consists of various themed areas that are linked to each other with connectors that have an urban look, and the enemies are spread around in them by random. But they are not designed in a way to prevent repetition. The areas will always have the exact same layout and enemy encounter locations, no matter if you use either the fixed or randomized level routes. The connectors consist of exact same buildings randomly (and sometimes even haphazardly) placed next to each other. And the enemies? There's a very limited number of enemy types. They do look different from each other, but function the same. What's worse, is that there's not much offered here to invoke a satisfying sense of progression either. You unlock new things by picking them up through a run, breaking boxes that contain floppy discs, or killing specific enemies; And nearly all of these are one-time collectables that require you to find hidden areas and be able to get far enough into the game. And while you keep getting new messages from other NPCs in the beginning hours in an attempt to have some story narration going on, the game just stops doing it after hitting a certain point and stays like that. [h2]I appreciate it, but why?[/h2] There are other things in the game that I feel like their inclusion was unnecessary. Take the difficulty modes for example. They are a normal addition in many games, but the problem is that the higher the difficulty is, the longer it will take for a normal player to beat this game. Coupled with the repetitive nature of the game, it can have a detrimental effect on the player's experience and have them going for lower difficulties in order to beat the game faster and be done with it. Therefore, maybe focusing on only one, pre-determined difficulty setting would have been better here; Especially since no achievements are tied to the difficulty. Then we have the checkpoint/banking system. Through your run, you have the option of keeping the money you have accumulated to buy mid-run upgrades, or transfer whatever you have on hand to the main hub through a checkpoint. If you bank a total of 500$, you will activate a save point that will give you a one-time chance to continue the game from that point after death. But what's the point? Most of the checkpoints, especially those in mid and late game, are useless as you will be forced to continue your run with starter stats and weapons. At that point, it would make more sense to start a new run. All of what I've said so far, makes me think that maybe the game should not have been a roguelite. Can it be improved to prevent the players from feeling bored, especially in early game? Yes. Absolutely. But with the way everything is designed here, I don't think such thing is possible right now. It would require a lot of work and quite possibly reworks of the game's code, which even myself would not want to do. Maybe going for a traditional FPS would have been the best choice as in my opinion, as the game does have what it takes to become something like its inspiration source. Maybe a classic system of having multiple episodes, each with their own levels and endings would have worked better. But alas, this has not happened and has left me with a game that I sadly cannot recommend. Still, if it turns out that a sequel in the works, I would be more than happy to play that and see what it can become, as I like what is offered here and love to see how it can be improved upon. [h2]TL;DR[/h2] There's a whole bunch of stuff to like in the game. However, the level design and the amount of available content cannot support its roguelite structure, quickly resulting in repetition and boredom.

I enjoyed this game at first but after playing it much longer I've realized how insultingly bad it is. It's environments aren't actually random at all, they always have the same layout, just in a different order if you chose it as an option, and the connecting areas just have random tiles where you can occasionally get health and armor. The boss fights might as well not exist because they are too easy and not fun at all, they just serve as an annoying threshold to cross. In order to fight the final boss you have to get to the end of the run like 6 times, making the game feel like a repetitive, mind numbing slog. The hero power that is also the name of the game, you only get to use for one run, and all it does is give you infinite armor for a short period of time and reset your health and it takes a very long time to charge up. Most of the weapons are annoying to use or just boring, with sounds that are too loud and overlap. The whole lewd aspect of the game is way overdone, with soft core porn plastered absolutely everywhere to the point where it detracts from the otherwise very nice and colorful retro art style, and genuinely nice environments. I get that it's basically supposed to parody this stuff but holy cow is it heavy handed with it.
